newsitem.title: USA: Pratt says opposes professional union.
newsitem.headline: Pratt says opposes professional union.

text.p: Jet engine maker Pratt & Whitney, a United Technologies Corp unit, said Tuesday it disapproved of an effort by engineers and technical personnel in its Florida unit to form their own professional union.
"We do not think it is in the best interests of the company or employees to have a union for our professional ranks," Pratt spokesman Bob Carroll told Reuters.

"It would make it more difficult for us to run the business, it takes away individuality of the individual, and it would probably impact our competitive posture on the world marketplace," Carroll said.

The Manchester, Conn., Journal Inquirer reported on Tuesday that the unionizing efforts within Pratt were partly in response to the company's Feb 7 layoffs of 450 non-union workers in Connecticut and Florida.
The report said the organizing effort, which began last year, has sparked interest among Pratt's Connecticut engineers as well.
Pratt has about 12,200 employees in Connecticut and 4,900 at its West Palm Beach, Fla., operations.

The report cited unnamed Pratt sources who said the company intends to slash up to 2,500 white-collar workers, including up to 1,500 in Connecticut. It said the layoffs were likely to occur in small groups through June.
Carroll said Pratt plans more layoffs but he gave no timeframe or numbers.
"Layoffs will continue until we become competitive on the world marketplace," he said.
